panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: cacheRead / (cacheRead + input). Higher = lower spend.

panels.title: Cost per accepted edit
panels.description: USD spent per accepted Edit/Write/MultiEdit. The closest thing to ROI.

panels.title: Sessions (window)
panels.description: Counts session starts. Resumed sessions don't increment.

panels.title: Cost per session
panels.description: Total spend / session starts in window. ROI per task.

panels.title: Cache savings $ (approx)
panels.description: Estimated USD avoided by cache reads vs paying full input price. Tune $/MTok dashboard variable to your model. Net = 0.9·cacheRead − 1.25·cacheCreation, scaled by input price.

panels.title: Edit accept rate
panels.description: % of code-edit suggestions accepted. Trust regression detector.

panels.title: Active time
panels.description: Total wall-clock time Claude was actively running (CLI).

panels.title: Cost rate by effort tier ($/hour)
panels.description: How much you spend at each thinking-effort level. xhigh is usually the biggest knob.

panels.title: API request latency p50/p95/p99 (ms) by model
panels.description: Latency quantiles from claude_code.api_request log events. Catches model-routing slow days.

panels.title: Tool result size p95 (bytes) by tool
panels.description: How much context each tool consumes back. Find the tools eating your budget.

panels.title: Activity heatmap (active seconds / 5m bucket)
panels.description: Density of CLI active time over your week. Tall stripes = focus blocks; gaps = downtime.

panels.title: Edits accepted by language (window)
panels.description: Where Claude is actually working in your repos.

panels.title: Auxiliary vs main spend
panels.description: Auxiliary = subagents and background tasks; main = your direct prompts. Big auxiliary share = subagent-heavy workflow.

panels.title: Auxiliary cost (subagent proxy)
panels.description: Top auxiliary spend by model + effort. True per-subagent attribution requires Tempo traces — open Explore → Tempo and run TraceQL once Claude Code emits spans.

panels.title: Cognitive throughput (output tokens / sec) by effort tier
panels.description: Output tokens generated per second of API request time, grouped by thinking-effort tier. Drops when the agent is wrestling a hard problem; rises in flow. The drop-with-effort-rise pattern is the closest telemetry signature of 'the brain working harder'.

targets.expr: 1000 * (sum by (effort) (sum_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name = `api_request` | unwrap output_tokens [5m])) / sum by (effort) (sum_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name = `api_request` | unwrap duration_ms [5m])))

panels.title: Tool-decision Shannon entropy (bits)
panels.description: Diversity of tool usage in a 5m window. 0 = stuck on one tool (loop / dead end). log2(N) = uniform across N distinct tools (broad exploration). Sudden collapses are the signature of a thought-loop.

panels.title: Per-query_source breakdown (background agents vs main thread)
Cost rate by query_source ($/hour)
panels.description: Burn rate for each internal Claude agent: repl_main_thread (your prompts), generate_session_title, away_summary, prompt_suggestion. Background agents should stay tiny vs. main.

panels.title: API request rate by query_source (req/min)
panels.description: Frequency of each internal agent. Sudden spikes in non-repl_main_thread sources can indicate retry loops.

panels.title: Latency p95 (ms) by query_source
panels.description: Per-agent response time. Background agents should be much faster; main thread should be slowest.

panels.title: Per-query_source totals (window)
panels.description: Aggregated metrics per internal agent over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Cost per turn — distribution
panels.description: Histogram of total $-cost per user prompt (grouped by prompt_id). The long right tail is where most of the budget goes — these are the prompts to optimize first.

panels.title: Tool calls per turn — distribution
panels.description: Histogram of #tool_decision events per user prompt. Low fan-out = quick lookups; high fan-out = deep multi-step reasoning. Watch for runaway tail.

panels.title: Cumulative cost per session ($)
panels.description: Running total spent per session over time. Shows when sessions turn expensive — often late, when context bloats and cache thrashes.

panels.title: User-prompt rhythm (prompts / min)
panels.description: Rate of user_prompt events. Spikes = chatty/paired moments; flat zero = thinking or AFK. Footer shows mean.

panels.title: Prompt length (chars) — distribution
panels.description: Histogram of how many characters each user_prompt contains. Bimodal usually — short clarifications vs. long structured tasks. Compare against cost-per-turn shape.

panels.title: Stuck-turn detector (high requests, low accepted edits)
panels.description: Per-prompt fan-out vs. productive output. Sorted by 'thrash ratio' = api_requests / (accepted_edits + 1). High = the agent went on a hunt without converting it into accepted code changes. Edits column is 0 for prompts that did no Edit/Write/MultiEdit (e.g. pure exploration or a Bash-heavy diagnostic).

targets.expr: sum by (prompt_id) (  count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"}    | event_name = `tool_decision`    | decision = `accept`    | tool_name =~ `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` [$__range])) or (sum by (prompt_id) (  count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name = `api_request` [$__range])) * 0)

panels.title: Recent agent traces — click → flame graph
panels.description: Synthesized OTLP traces from Claude Code log events (one per prompt_id). Each row links to Tempo's native flame-graph view. The synthesizer at hooks/agent-flame/sync.py emits a trace ~60s after a prompt goes idle.

panels.title: Latency detective — API requests sorted by duration (outliers in red)
panels.description: Each row = one Claude API request from Loki log events. Sorted by duration_ms desc; rows above 30 s are highlighted as outliers. Click any column header to re-sort. The right-hand ratio column (ms_per_token) is the strongest signal — high ratio means lots of thinking for little visible output.
